title: Security and Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, Risk & Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This consolidated guidance describes Redwood Inference's mandatory controls and operational workflows across seven security and compliance pillars: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. This document is intended for engineers, product managers, security reviewers, and compliance owners.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood-managed control plane components, hosted inference endpoints, Dedicated and Private deployment packages, and supporting infrastructure (CI/CD, observability, identity systems).
- Excludes ephemeral developer sandbox projects unless explicitly onboarded to production controls.

Owner and escalation:
- Security Owner: Aisha Patel (security@redwood.example.com)
- Primary Engineering Contact: Marcus Li (eng-platform@redwood.example.com)
- Compliance & Audit Lead: Priya Sharma (compliance@redwood.example.com)

---

1) RBAC & Authentication

Goal:
Ensure least-privilege access to control plane, admin consoles, and data stores; enforce strong authentication and automated provisioning/deprovisioning.

Core controls:
- Identity provider: All user and service authentication is delegated to the corporate OIDC provider (Okta). No service or interactive accounts should bypass the IdP without an approved exception.
- Roles & groups: Standardized role set (admin, infra-operator, svc-account, developer-readonly, product-analyst). Teams must map to these roles before production onboarding.
- Service accounts: Short-lived tokens (maximum TTL 24h) are issued to workloads via the workload identity system. Long-lived API keys are prohibited except where explicitly approved by security.
- MFA: Mandatory for all interactive accounts with admin or infra-operator roles.
- Privileged access review: Quarterly attestation process run by Compliance (list of privileged accounts, last attested date).

Provisioning and deprovisioning process:
1. All new hires are granted baseline developer-readonly via HR -> Okta sync.
2. Team owners submit access requests using the Access Request form (link in Squad onboarding).
3. Access approvers (team leads + security) must approve within 72 hours.
4. Offboarding is automated via HR event webhooks; security must confirm service account rotations within 24 hours of offboard.

Role enforcement and technical implementation:
- Kubernetes: Roles enforced via RBAC and mapped to OIDC groups. Admin actions require time-limited elevation through a Just-In-Time (JIT) access service.
- Cloud console/console APIs: IAM policies are narrowly scoped to resource tags (env:prod, owner_team).
- Secrets management: All secrets live in the centralized KMS-backed vault. Access is gated by roles and require approval for create/read operations.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Access review completion: 95% of privileged accounts attested within 7 days of quarterly run.
- Deprovisioning lag: 0% of terminated users with access after 48 hours (target).

---

2) Audit Logging

Goal:
Collect, retain, and protect immutable audit logs sufficient for forensic investigation and compliance evidence.

Logging sources and minimum retention:
- Sources: IdP auth events, API gateway requests, model inference request metadata (control plane only; payloads redacted), admin console actions, infrastructure orchestration (Terraform apply), and vault access.
- Minimum retention: 1 year for high-sensitivity logs (auth, admin actions), 13 months for general operational logs to support annual audits. Longer retention for customers under contract is handled per Data Residency & Retention policy.

Format and protection:
- All audit logs must be written in structured JSON with timestamp (ISO 8601), actor, action, resource, request_id, and outcome.
- Immutable storage: Logs are written to append-only storage (WORM) and replicated across two regions for availability.
- Integrity: Periodic hash chaining and tamper-detection checks (daily) are performed and recorded.

Alerting and monitoring:
- High-priority alerts: multiple failed admin authentications, privilege escalation events, bulk export attempts of audit logs.
- Alert SLA: Security ops triage within 30 minutes for P1 alerts, acknowledge within 15 minutes when oncall.

Access to logs:
- Only security and SRE teams have read access by default. Access for other teams requires a documented investigation request and time-limited RBAC grant.

---

3) Data Residency & Retention

Goal:
Enforce customer and regulatory requirements for where data is stored and how long it is retained.

Residency controls:
- Region tagging: All customer datasets and backups are tagged with data_residency (e.g., eu, us, apac).
- Deployment modes: Hosted customers select a region at onboarding; Dedicated and Private deployments must document physical location of storage and compute.
- Cross-border transfers: Explicit treaties & DPA clauses required; transfers are logged and approved by Legal.

Retention & deletion:
- Default retention for control-plane metadata: 13 months.
- Customer-configurable retention for inference logs/payloads: 30 days (default), configurable to 0 (ephemeral) or up to contract limits.
- Deletion process:
  1) Customer requests deletion via console or support ticket.
  2) Automated workflow verifies scope and submits deletion job to object-store lifecycle manager.
  3) Deletion is logged to audit stream and a signed attestation is provided to the customer.

Encryption and key management:
- Data at rest: AES-256.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported for Private deployments; hosted customers may opt for Redwood-managed keys with clear SLAs.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Deletion job completion: 95% of deletion requests completed within 48 hours.

---

4) Secure SDLC

Goal:
Baked-in security requirements across design, development, and deployment to reduce vulnerability introduction and accelerate secure delivery.

Mandatory phases and artifacts:
- Design review: Every change touching the control plane, auth, logging, or data flows requires a security design review (SDR) before implementation.
- Threat modeling: Required for new services and major architecture changes; use the standard STRIDE template.
- Static and dynamic scanning: PR-level SAST (fail-on-high), periodic DAST for public endpoints, and dependency vulnerability scanning (weekly).
- Secrets scanning: Pre-merge check and runtime detection for leaked credentials.
- CI/CD gating: Security checks and compliance checks are enforced in pipeline. No direct deploy to prod without passing the gate.

Release controls:
- Canary & progressive rollouts: New control-plane features must roll out via canary (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated health checks and automatic rollback on regression.
- Post-deploy review: Every production rollout must include an owner-signed checklist verifying security gating criteria.

Metrics and reporting:
- Mean time to remediate critical findings: <= 7 days.
- PRs blocked by security checks: tracked monthly with triage notes.

---

5) Incident Response: Security Procedures

Goal:
Ensure coordinated detection, containment, eradication, and post-incident evidence collection aligned with compliance timelines.

Detection and triage:
- Sources: SIEM alerts, SRE/observability alerts, external reports.
- Triage owner: Oncall secops or SRE depending on event type.

Immediate actions (first 60 minutes):
1. Triage call initiated with security, SRE, product owner, and legal (if customer-impacting).
2. Capture volatile evidence: snapshot ephemeral logs, record system state, preserve memory dumps where allowed.
3. Implement containment: rotate affected credentials, revoke sessions, isolate compromised instances.
4. Notify customers per contractual obligations if exfiltration or availability impacts are confirmed.

Forensic evidence handling:
- Preserve chain-of-custody: log who accessed evidence, time, and reason.
- Duplicate logs to an isolated evidence bucket with restricted access.
- Maintain an incident dossier (standard template) that includes timeline, impact assessment, and IOC list.

Post-incident activities:
- Root cause analysis and action item tracking with owners and due dates.
- Update runbooks and playbooks within 5 business days of incident closure.
- Executive and regulatory reporting: compile required evidence and certifications within contract SLA windows.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Incident detection-to-acknowledge: within 15 minutes for P1.
- Initial containment objective: within 2 hours for confirmed breaches.

---

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Goal:
Provide auditable, repeatable evidence packages for internal and external audits (SOC2, ISO27001, contractual audits).

Evidence collection patterns:
- Mapping matrix: Each control maps to one or more evidence artifacts (policy docs, config snapshots, logs, access attestations, runbook signatures).
- Evidence storage: Centralized evidence repository with immutable versions and access logging.

Typical evidence artifacts:
- RBAC: role definitions, recent access review attestation, sample IAM policy JSONs.
- Audit logging: retention config, sample logs (redacted), integrity check reports.
- SDLC: threat model exports, SAST/DAST reports, CI/CD pipeline audit trail.
- Incident response: incident dossier, timeline, remediation actions, communication logs.

Evidence request process:
1. Auditor or internal reviewer submits request to compliance@redwood.example.com.
2. Compliance owner validates scope and compiles artifact set.
3. Evidence package delivered with hash-sum and access log.

Retention of evidence:
- Audit evidence retained for 3 years unless contractually required longer.

---

7) Risk & Exceptions

Goal:
Provide a documented exception process for temporary or compensating controls while minimizing risk exposure.

Exception workflow:
1. Request: Team submits exception request form with justification, duration, and compensating controls.
2. Review: Security + Risk committee evaluates risk and either deny, approve, or approve with conditions.
3. Approval: Approved exceptions are timeboxed (max 90 days) and tracked in the exception register.
4. Renewal: Requests to renew must include remediation progress and executive sponsor sign-off.

Compensating controls examples:
- If long-lived key required temporarily, require IP-restriction of key usage and enhanced audit sampling.
- If temporary elevated access granted, enforce session recording and limit to a single session per approver.

Risk acceptance thresholds:
- High risk: requires SOC or CISO approval and legal notification.
- Medium risk: Requires security director approval.
- Low risk: Can be approved by the engineering security lead.

---

Ownership, KPIs and Review Cadence

Responsibilities:
- Security: policy and control owners, quarterly reviews.
- Eng SRE: operationalizing logging, alerting, incident runbooks.
- Compliance: evidence packages and audit coordination.

KPIs:
- Privileged access review coverage: >= 95% on each quarterly run.
- Audit log integrity check failures: 0 per month target.
- Time to close critical SDLC findings: <= 7 days.

Review cadence:
- Quarterly policy review by Security and Compliance.
- Annual tabletop incident simulation with cross-functional participants.

---

Appendix: Sample artifacts and snippets

1) Example minimal audit log JSON (redacted):
```
{
  "ts":"2026-09-30T15:22:10Z",
  "actor":"user:marcus.li@redwood.example.com",
  "action":"iam:policy.update",
  "resource":"/projects/prod/iam/policies/xyz",
  "request_id":"req-1234567890",
  "outcome":"success"
}
```

2) Checklist: Production Onboarding Security Gate (sample)
- [ ] IdP mapping configured
- [ ] Service accounts created with required TTL
- [ ] Audit log forwarding enabled and retention verified
- [ ] Data residency tag set and encryption verified
- [ ] SDLC threat model completed
- [ ] Incident contact and escalation confirmed
- [ ] Compliance evidence artifacts indexed

3) Exception register sample (CSV-style):
owner,component,exception_reason,approved_by,expires_at
engineering-team-foo,control-plane-api,legacy-service-key,security-director,2026-12-01
